profile.address: 2151 Mission College Blvd, Santa Clara, CA 95054
profile.reading: Per Evocative own site, this Santa Clara, California facility (SJC11) sits at 2151 Mission College Blvd and totals 73,000 square feet, with 9 MW of total power capacity delivered as two 4.5 MW feeds from diverse substations. Evocative's own page for SJC11 further describes 2 x 1,200 ton Baltimore Air Coil cooling units with 4 x 75 horsepower pumps, a 5 x 750 kVA UPS system in an N+1 design, and 4 x 1.5 MW Caterpillar generators backing the facility. The operator's own page states this building was originally an Intel network operations center and satellite facility that has since been completely updated for colocation use. The operator lists compliance with HIPAA, PCI DSS, SOC 2 Type II, SOC 3, ISAE 3402, SSAE 18, LEED, and Green Globes standards, and describes direct fiber connectivity to San Francisco along with multiple carrier options including AT&T, Lumen, Cogent, and Verizon, serving a population of roughly 11.9 million people within 100 miles. Evocative describes itself as a global infrastructure provider operating data center, bare metal, network, cloud, and managed services across 24 data centers in 14 metros, with this Santa Clara building one of two Evocative facilities in the South Bay alongside a separate SJC14 building. Santa Clara, California is headquarters to Intel Corporation and sits at the center of Silicon Valley's dense data center and technology corridor, alongside major colocation campuses operated by Equinix, Digital Realty, and CoreSite in the same city. The area draws power from Silicon Valley Power, the city owned municipal utility, and from Pacific Gas and Electric in surrounding areas, both interconnected to the CAISO grid that also serves much of central and northern California. Evocative, a national colocation operator, has built part of its portfolio through acquisitions of smaller regional colocation operators, consolidating facilities like this former Intel site into a unified network branded under the Evocative name.

profile.reading: Evocative Secaucus, branded EWR1 on the operator's own site, is a data center in Secaucus, New Jersey. Evocative's own dedicated page for this facility, fetched directly from evocative.com, gives an address of 1 Enterprise Avenue N, Secaucus, New Jersey 07094, superseding this row's earlier reverse geocoded approximation, and describes a 105,000 square foot facility with 10 megawatts of total power capacity delivered as two 5 megawatt diverse underground feeds, expandable to 20 megawatts. The operator's own page lists 4 x 400 ton air cooled chillers in an N+1 design, 4 x 1.4 megawatt APC Symmetra UPS systems, and 4 x 2 megawatt generators in an N+1 configuration rated for 48 hours at full load. The page states the site sits outside the 500 year flood plain and within 100 miles of approximately 31.2 million people, and describes direct fiber access to a nearby Equinix campus less than a mile away. Evocative's own page lists compliance with HIPAA, PCI DSS, SOC 2 Type II, SOC 3, ISAE 3402, and SSAE 18 standards. Evocative describes itself elsewhere on its site as a global infrastructure provider operating data center, bare metal, network, cloud, and managed services across 24 data centers in 14 strategically located metros and 32 points of presence, with this Secaucus building serving the New York metro market alongside other Evocative locations in California, Arizona, Georgia, Massachusetts, Texas, and Washington already on file elsewhere in this registry. Secaucus sits in the Hudson County data center corridor across the river from Manhattan, a market anchored by major carrier hotel and colocation campuses including Equinix's Secaucus buildings and other operators drawn by proximity to New York financial and media firms along with lower New Jersey real estate and power costs relative to Manhattan itself.

reading.body:
Evocative operates a single confirmed facility with published power capacity: Santa Clara, California, with 9 MW across 73,000 square feet, while two additional US locations lack published capacity figures.

The operator describes itself as a colocation provider with 10 US data centers spanning seven states and eight international points of presence. Its CEO since February 2017, Arman Khalili, came from founding two prior infrastructure companies and leading Black Lotus before its acquisition by Level 3 Communications. Under Khalili, Evocative acquired Emeryville and San Jose facilities from 365 Data Centers around 2017, notably repurchasing Emeryville after selling it to 365 Main in 2013. The company's expansion pattern reflects consolidation common in colocation, where facilities rotate between operators rather than new construction.

The Santa Clara facility holds dual 4.5 MW feeds from separate substations and maintains SOC 2 Type 2, PCI DSS, HIPAA, SSAE 18, LEED, and Green Globes certifications. At 9 MW total for 73,000 square feet, this yields approximately 0.123 MW per thousand square feet, typical for colocation serving enterprise rather than hyperscale workloads. Neither the New Jersey nor Virginia facilities had published capacity or square footage at the time of research, limiting visibility into Evocative's true power footprint.

The registry entry here covers only three locations. Evocative's stated portfolio of ten US data centers means seven remain untracked, and the Virginia facility does not appear on the operator's own site, indicating either stale registry data or a location the company no longer lists or serves. Without headquarters address, founding year, or current ownership information from primary sources, financial trajectory and current capitalization remain opaque.
